question.text: Which of the following is NOT part of a Portfolio Manager's core regulatory obligations?

answer.text: Pre-clearance of personal trades under the insider-trading code
Assuring a fixed return to clients in marketing communications

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook's code of conduct and marketing rules prohibit portfolio managers from making any statement or becoming privy to any act, practice or unfair competition that is likely to be harmful to investors' interests, including assurances of returns. KYC, record maintenance and PIT pre-clearance, by contrast, are explicit obligations on the portfolio manager. The Trap: KYC on-boarding, record maintenance and PIT pre-clearance are all source-supported regulatory duties. The exception is the marketing practice — assuring returns is a prohibited conduct rather than a core obligation. Note: Identify what the workbook lists as an obligation versus what it lists as a prohibited practice. Assured returns fall in the prohibited bucket.
